learning_objective: 🎯 Explore the microscopic bustling city of the cell! Understand the specific structure and crucial function of each cellular organelle.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Described by the Fluid Mosaic Model (Singer & Nicolson). It's a dynamic, semi-permeable lipid bilayer with embedded proteins that controls what enters and exits the cell.
Contains the cell's genetic material (DNA). It is enclosed by a double membrane with nuclear pores that regulate the transport of RNA and proteins.
A coordinated system including the Endoplasmic Reticulum (ER - makes proteins/lipids), Golgi apparatus (packages and modifies them), and Lysosomes (cellular waste disposal/suicide bags).
A double-membrane organelle where cellular respiration occurs, generating ATP (energy). It has its own circular DNA and ribosomes, making it semi-autonomous.
Found in plants and algae. Contains chlorophyll for photosynthesis. Like mitochondria, it is double-membraned and has its own DNA.

fun_activity.title: 🏙️ The Cell City
fun_activity.instructions: Imagine a cell is a city. Match the organelle to its city job: Nucleus = City Hall, Mitochondria = Power Plant, Lysosome = Garbage Disposal, Golgi = Post Office. Draw your own Cell City map!

exam_tips: 📌 The Endomembrane system only includes ER, Golgi, Lysosomes, and Vacuoles because their functions are coordinated. Mitochondria and chloroplasts are NOT part of it.
📌 Smooth ER (SER) synthesizes lipids, while Rough ER (RER) has ribosomes and synthesizes proteins.
📌 Remember the 'Endosymbiotic Theory'—mitochondria and chloroplasts were likely once free-living bacteria because they have their own circular DNA and 70S ribosomes.
quick_recap: ⭐ The Fluid Mosaic Model explains that the cell membrane is flexible like a fluid, with protein 'icebergs' floating in a lipid 'sea'.
⭐ Plant cells have a rigid cell wall (made of cellulose) outside the plasma membrane; animal cells do not.
⭐ Ribosomes are non-membrane bound organelles found in both eukaryotes and prokaryotes.
